summary: Ordinary invoke/stream/readiness share one HTTP transport; extraction uses a fixed pure data client tool with server-side native denial proven on a pinned local Gateway; cron accepts only exact job/run completion within one deadline.

operator_clarification.scope: A pinned reproducible local/dev Gateway with a synthetic model or no-auth test route may satisfy functional acceptance. No real account credentials or authenticated external Gateway required. Tool/tenant safety and 100-request CLI/HTTP benchmark remain required.

changes: Removed ordinary CLI invocation, argv size routing, and the unused CLI reply decoder; administrative cron/auth CLI and read-only kernel delegation retained.
One HTTP builder preserves admitted agent/model, scoped session, messages/context/attachments, trace, errors, usage, and terminal outcome.
Readiness no longer falls back to another model; a previous explicit override cannot change subsequent ordinary routing.
Restricted emit_extraction schema and argument validation reject invalid or unexpected tools; native tools are separately denied in the pinned Gateway fixture.

Cron uses exact id/runId lookup and requires both jobId and runId in the returned entry. Missing run ID, late results, failed/cancelled/skipped runs and real hung subprocess fail without resubmission.
Fixed test_cron.py canonical package imports so the previously excluded cron suite now runs.

P1 correction: invoke and stream share conversation resolution: internal explicit session ID, metadata.session_user, then legacy metadata.session_id. Tenant/actor escaping and positional identity remain unchanged.

P2 correction: one effective-model resolver is used by invoke, stream and readiness. Main-agent defaults resolve to OPENCLAW_PRIMARY_MODEL/provider default; non-default agents retain their Gateway model unless an admitted explicit override is supplied.

Mounted HTTP regressions prove conversation continuity/isolation, session alias precedence, identical default model headers including readiness, and preservation of admitted explicit/agent-configured models.

P1 correction for b643c5fa: invoke and stream now share the durable Persona ledger with atomic actor-bound claims, cross-route terminal replay, in-doubt fencing, and admitted tenant/actor/pint session identity. Streaming persists its terminal envelope before publishing it and forwards first-attempt deltas.

Structured endpoint reads config.get on the same authenticated Gateway before every dispatch; valid exact-agent tools.deny=["*"] is required. Missing, ambiguous, malformed or unavailable policy denies before model execution. Policy RPC and HTTP share one total deadline.

Replaced fixed replay spawn values with actual CPython Popen audit events attributed to each concurrent arm/case; extra real subprocesses fail the replay count gate. Executed a fresh complete 100-pair replay with frozen inputs.
implementation.post_measurement_change: Provider bytes remain identical to the recorded 100-pair replay. main.py now shares the existing Persona durable ledger across mounted invoke/stream routes; those changes are validated by mounted real-provider HTTP fixtures and SQLite fault/concurrency regressions, not by the provider-only replay. The mounted structured endpoint now also verifies live native-tool denial through administrative config.get before invoking the unchanged HTTP provider. This additional extraction admission is covered by mounted pinned-Gateway probes and full regressions, not by ordinary-turn benchmark timing.
implementation.ownership_recovery: Canonical supervisor recovery on 2026-09-06 reassigned owner to Codex2 and reviewer to Codex. Earlier source authors and historical reviewer findings remain identified by their original commits.

coverage: All four invoke/stream first-attempt and replay combinations issue exactly one upstream HTTP request, preserve text/usage/response ID and use admitted tenant, authenticated actor and normalized pint identity.

Failed terminals replay as errors, never done; missing usage remains absent and JSON opinion text is replayed verbatim.
Mounted generator crash and failed terminal persistence publish no done; both routes fence subsequent attempts in_doubt.
Partial-stream generator cancellation closes its upstream iterator and leaves the persistent claim in_doubt.
Four cross-route concurrency combinations fence the competing request; four simultaneous SQLite claims yield one winner and three typed in_doubt results.
Typed 401/429/503/504 failures retain status code, error code and message across both routes without a second provider call.
